text:
jamal: hey team — first week, hit a weird one. i switch to our prod-ish context with `kubectl config use-context prod-usw2` but a few commands later i'm back in my laptop dev context. i noticed a `.envrc` in the repo and some okta/awsvault helpers. macbook, zsh. any quick fixes?

Priya (DevEx): welcome Jamal! :wave: common cause: multiple kubeconfigs or a background tool (okta/awsvault/direnv) re-exporting KUBECONFIG. run `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config get-contexts` and paste outputs.

jamal: `echo $KUBECONFIG` -> `/Users/jamal/.kube/config:/Users/jamal/.kube/okta` and `kubectl config get-contexts` shows dev-usw2 * and prod-usw2. switching works but after `make deploy` it flips.

Lucas (Infra): sounds like a deploy script or okta helper is rewriting the file. check for post-deploy hooks that call `aws sso`, `okta-aws`, or `aws-iam-authenticator`. also see if `.envrc` contains `export KUBECONFIG=...` — direnv will set it when you cd.

direnv-bot: .envrc detected in repo root. content snippet: `export KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/dev:$HOME/.kube/okta` — requires `direnv allow` to activate.

jamal: ah — i didn't `direnv allow`. so when i cd the KUBECONFIG gets reset. if i allow it, will that permanently force dev context? i want to run ephemeral prod-only commands for smoke tests.

Priya (DevEx): don't allow if you don't want it. two options: 1) flatten a prod-only kubeconfig for the session: `kubectl config use-context prod-usw2; kubectl config view --minify --flatten > ~/.kube/prod-session; export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/prod-session` 2) create a tiny wrapper script `with-prod-kube.sh` that sets KUBECONFIG for a single command.

Lucas (Infra): for running jobs as the CI SA: check if cluster supports `kubectl -n prod create token ci-bot --duration=15m`. if not, infra can mint a short-lived service token for you. also, for namespace RBAC requests, send this: `cluster: prod-usw2, namespace: prod-team-b, subject: jamal, verbs: get,list,create,patch,delete (only if needed), resources: jobs,pods,events, reason: run local smoke CI, duration: 14d`. include your RedToken.

jamal: thanks. one quick safety Q — i'm worried about accidentally committing the prod-only kubeconfig file. any guardrails?

Priya (DevEx): add `~/.kube/*.session` or the specific filename to your global gitignore, and never keep tokens in files tracked by git. our git hooks also block commits with `kubeconfig` or `Bearer ` in plaintext but don't rely on that.

Lucas (Infra): i'll approve a short grant for you and generate a one-time token if `kubectl create token` isn't allowed. tagging @eng-security for audit logging — we rotate tokens and will log the grant. expect a ping here when done.

jamal: awesome — i'll hold off on `direnv allow` and try the wrapper script. thanks y'all!

Priya (DevEx): welcome aboard again! ping for a quick screenshare if you want us to walk through the token/flattening steps. :coffee:
